title: Module 6: ROI Scoring with the MetaMetrics Index
description: Tests the rep's fluency with the MMI formula, the four input dimensions (Time, Cost, Quality, Satisfaction), the TSS and IE multipliers, and the ability to compare workflows by score.
instructions: Answer all questions to the best of your ability. The MMI formula is (TSS / IE) × (Time + Cost + Quality + Satisfaction), with each input rated 1-5. You cannot ask ARC for help while the quiz is in progress. Aim for 10-12 minutes.

questions.prompt: What does the 'TSS / IE' multiplier represent in the MMI formula?

options.label: Total Sales Score divided by Industry Estimate
Task Strategic Significance divided by Implementation Effort — how much the workflow matters scaled against how hard it is to build
Time Spent Saved divided by Initial Expense
Total Sentiment Score divided by Internal Evaluation

questions.explanation: TSS / IE is the multiplier that adjusts the raw dimensional sum based on strategic value relative to build difficulty. A workflow with high strategic significance (TSS=5) and low implementation effort (IE=1) gets a 5× multiplier on its (T+C+Q+S) sum — making it a Priority One target. Inverting that (TSS=1, IE=5) yields a 0.2× multiplier, demoting the workflow. This is how AEGISAXIOM surfaces the highest-leverage automations first.

questions.prompt: Calculate the MMI score for this workflow: TSS=5, IE=1, Time=4, Cost=4, Quality=3, Satisfaction=3.
questions.explanation: The math: (TSS/IE) × (T+C+Q+S) = (5/1) × (4+4+3+3) = 5 × 14 = 70. This is a Priority One workflow — high strategic value, easy to implement, strong dimensional contributions across the board. You'd put this at the top of the AI Employee Matrix and lead with it in the SOW.

questions.prompt: Which of the following workflows would you EXPECT to score highest on the Time dimension?

options.label: A monthly task that takes 10 minutes once a month
A daily task that takes 4 hours and currently consumes a full headcount
A one-off project that takes 80 hours but never repeats
A real-time alert system that runs in milliseconds

questions.explanation: B. The Time dimension measures velocity — the gap between human time spent and the agent's execution time, multiplied by frequency. A high-frequency, high-duration manual task (like option B's 4 hours/day) generates massive Time-dimension savings when automated. A is too low-frequency, C is non-recurring, D is already fast. The signature of a high Time score is a worker doing 'the same thing over and over for a meaningful chunk of every day.'

questions.prompt: True or False: The Satisfaction dimension in MMI measures only external customer NPS — it doesn't include internal employee experience.
questions.explanation: False. Satisfaction is intentionally double-sided: it captures both external customer satisfaction (NPS, CSAT, churn risk) AND internal employee experience (the cost of tedium, retention risk on roles stuck doing soul-crushing manual work). A workflow that frees a senior analyst from copy-pasting all day scores high on Satisfaction even if no external customer ever notices the change. Reps who only frame Satisfaction as 'customer NPS' miss a huge portion of the ROI story.

questions.prompt: You have two workflows to recommend to a client. Workflow A: TSS=5, IE=2, T=3, C=3, Q=3, S=3 → score = (5/2) × 12 = 30. Workflow B: TSS=4, IE=1, T=3, C=2, Q=3, S=2 → score = (4/1) × 10 = 40. Which should you lead with in the SOW, and why?

options.label: Workflow A — it has the higher strategic significance (TSS=5)
Workflow B — it has the higher MMI score (40 vs 30), meaning the lower implementation effort outweighs A's higher TSS for total ROI ranking
Workflow A — its dimensional sum (12) is higher
Either — the difference is too small to matter

questions.explanation: B is correct, and this is the central insight of MMI: raw strategic importance does NOT win — the SCORE wins. Workflow A is more strategically significant in isolation (TSS=5 vs 4), but its higher implementation effort (IE=2) cuts the multiplier in half. Workflow B's lower IE more than compensates. This is why we always sort the AI Employee Matrix by MMI score, not by any single input. A 'quick win' workflow can absolutely outrank a 'big strategic project' for ROI — and clients respect reps who lead with the math.

questions.prompt: Match each client signal to the MMI dimension it most directly affects.

items.label: Our outbound team makes the same data entry mistakes about 8% of the time, and we have to re-do orders
Our junior analysts have a 40% turnover rate, mostly because they hate the manual reporting work
We're paying three full-time contractors $90/hour each just to keep the spreadsheets in sync
Sales reps lose deals because they can't get a quote out faster than 48 hours

questions.explanation: i1 is Quality — error reduction is the textbook Quality signal. i2 is Satisfaction (internal employee retention angle). i3 is Cost — direct labor arbitrage on the contractors. i4 is Time — quote velocity directly drives the Time dimension. Notice that several of these workflows would actually score on multiple dimensions; the question asks for the MOST direct mapping.

questions.prompt: A client says: 'I don't really care about MMI scores — just tell me if this is going to save us money.' In two sentences, how do you respond?
questions.rubric: A passing answer (1) doesn't dismiss the client's concern, and (2) reframes MMI as the rigorous way to GET to a credible cost answer (not in opposition to it). Bonus credit for noting that scoring on all 4 dimensions surfaces savings the client hadn't considered (turnover, quality, opportunity cost). Penalize answers that lecture or get defensive about the methodology.
